descriptionChirho: To give something to someone as a gift, payment, or transfer of possession (Arabic root signal: أَعْطَى ʾaʿṭā 'to give'); the core and most frequent Qal sense of natan covering all inflections of basic giving.

To put, place, or set something in a spatial location including setting one's face or directing attention (Arabic root signal: وَضَعَ waḍaʿa 'to place'; Korean 놓다/두다 'to place'; Swahili -weka 'to put').
To make, render, or appoint someone or something into a new state or role (Arabic root signal: جَعَلَ jaʿala 'to make/render'; Korean 만들다 'to make'; Swahili -fanya 'to make').

To deliver, surrender, or hand over a person or thing into the power or custody of another, often in military or judicial contexts (Arabic root signal: سَلَّمَ sallama / أَسْلَمَ aslama 'to deliver/surrender'; Korean 넘겨주다 'to hand over').
To allow, permit, or let someone do something; to refrain from preventing an action (Arabic root signal: يَدَعُ yadaʿu 'to let/leave'; Korean 허락하다 'to permit'; Swahili -ruhusu 'to permit').
To give forth or utter sound, voice, or proclamation; natan used with qol or similar objects of vocal expression (Arabic root signal: أَعْلَنَ aʿlana 'to proclaim'; Swahili -tangaza 'to announce').

Nifal passive and Qal passive participle: to be given, be handed over, or be delivered; the passive counterpart covering both the giving and surrendering senses (Arabic passive يُعْطَى / يُسَلَّمُ; Korean 주어지다/넘겨지다 'to be given/handed over').
